screening_results.reason: This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (ages 24–37; N=10 for fMRI) using socially relevant non-verbal vocalizations and animated faces, addressing social-related perception/understanding of others. Group-level voxelwise statistical analyses (voxel-by-voxel two-tailed t tests, maps transformed to Talairach space, thresholded maps and ROI analyses) are presented as group activation maps (figures/tables), satisfying group whole-brain voxelwise reporting (not merely ROI-based). Healthy adult results are reported separately and clearly. Although slice coverage was focused on temporal cortex, the paper presents group voxelwise task-evoked activation maps and contrasts for the healthy sample, meeting the review’s requirements.

This is an fMRI study of prosody perception and production tied to social communication and empathy (social-related processing). Sample: 19 healthy, right-handed native-English adults aged 18–58 (within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., “happy-neutral”, “question-neutral”) thresholded and corrected (p<0.05 FDR, cluster k>5) and describes coordinates and supplementary materials; overlap/SVC and whole-brain contrasts are reported in text and figures. Results are clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. No evidence of ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range samples. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met.

This is an original fMRI study in healthy adult participants (students, mean age 25.7) that used a social-emotion task (guilt memories and hypothetical social scenarios) relevant to social cognition/perception of self and others. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (thresholded whole-brain maps at p<0.001 with cluster extent and reported activated regions and coordinates) as well as SVC results. The sample is within the 18–65 range and results for the healthy group are reported. The study is empirical fMRI (task-based) and not ROI-only or connectivity-only. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (mean age ~31) that uses the Ultimatum Game, a social economic exchange task probing social decision-making and cooperation. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (random-effects ANOVA, conjunction analyses, whole-brain parametric regressions) with coordinates and corrected statistics, clearly from the healthy participant groups. Methods and results provide whole-brain statistical maps and coordinate tables. Thus it meets the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

The study uses fMRI during social tasks in healthy adults (theory-of-mind and social attribution-of-attention) and meets I3 and I4. However, it does not report a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise activation map for the healthy group. Task-related analyses were performed using localized ICA within a TPJ ROI (ROI-limited task decomposition) and task relevance was assessed via IC time-course regressions; whole-brain results are limited to seed-to-voxel functional connectivity maps (connectivity, not task-evoked activation). Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain task activation reporting and meets exclusion criteria E2 and E3.

The study uses task fMRI during a social-related face encoding/recognition paradigm (meets I3) and includes healthy adult participants (young subgroup aged 20–31; meets I4). However, the imaging analyses reported are region-of-interest (amygdala) extractions and parameter estimates; the paper does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or whole-brain results for the healthy group. Because no unmasked whole-brain task effect for the healthy group is provided, the study fails inclusion criterion I5 and therefore must be excluded under exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–55) using an explicit social task (imitate/observe emotional faces) probing perception/understanding of others. The methods describe whole-brain preprocessing and group-level analyses (PLS and GLM) with voxelwise brain maps rendered in MNI space and thresholded voxel patterns reported, satisfying whole-brain task-evoked reporting. Healthy participant results are reported for the group (neuroimaging data from 20 participants used for final analysis). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social processing in healthy adults and provides whole-brain group-level task activation data.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (kinship/ moral dilemma) in healthy adults. It used whole-brain, task-based fMRI during an ecologically valid movie-viewing social/moral task and a separate moral-decision task. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=30, ages 19–39). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results from inter-subject correlation (ISC) analyses and a GLM analysis of the moral-decision task, with multiple-comparison correction and tables/figures of clusters and coordinates (and unthresholded maps referenced). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

The study is an fMRI task of social evaluation in healthy adult participants (meets I3 and I4). However, the manuscript reports group-level results that were small-volume corrected within a predefined vACC ROI and presents ROI-restricted activation clusters. There is no clear report of an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. Because the paper appears to report only ROI-restricted analyses without accompanying whole-brain task-evoked results, it violates the review requirement for whole-brain evidence (E2).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 21–48) that used an active task (viewing erotic pictures and videos of other people) engaging perception of others and reward-related/social-affiliative processing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (within-group male vs female stimulus contrasts for each orientation group) with corrected thresholds (p<0.05 FWE) and cluster reports, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The sample is healthy adults and results for the healthy groups are reported separately. Whole-brain results are presented in text, figures, and tables. No exclusion criterion (ROI-only, resting-state-only, age outside range, non-empirical) is violated. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of social interaction perception in healthy adults (ages 18–34). The tasks are social-related (perception/understanding of others) and functional MRI was used. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (interaction > independent actions) with FDR-corrected clusters and whole-brain analyses described in the text and figures. Whole-brain results are clearly reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using a social-cognition task (modified Empathic Accuracy Task) that involves perception and understanding of others’ emotions. The sample comprises healthy adults (final fMRI sample N=34, ages 20–30). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (random-effects paired t-tests, TFCE FWE-corrected results) with tables and figures of significant clusters. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for healthy adult fMRI whole-brain task activations and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This paper reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (three studies, combined N=59) performing social-related semantic tasks (person knowledge, socially relevant words), satisfying the review’s social-processing target. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are reported (e.g., social > non-social semantics) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction and peak coordinates presented, clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control participants; ROI analyses are supplementary. Study 2 includes control participants reported separately from patient data. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (1) It uses task-based fMRI during a social-related approach-avoidance task contrasting social vs nonsocial stimuli (relevant to social processing constructs); (2) Sample consists of healthy adults (male, mean age 21.35, N=76 analyzed) within the 18–65 range; (3) The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses and describes exploratory whole-brain results beyond ROI analyses (with reference to whole-brain results reported in the manuscript/supplement); (4) Whole-brain results are acceptable to be in supplementary materials per criteria. No exclusion criteria are violated (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, includes healthy adult task activation maps). Therefore INCLUDE.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (impression formation of faces varying by race and status) in healthy adult participants (N=60 males, mean age 23.8). The task is clearly social (impression formation), satisfying I3. The sample comprises healthy adults within 18–65, satisfying I4. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise multivariate PLS results (brain–behavior LVs) and displays/thresholds whole-brain voxel maps and cluster reports; GLM preprocessing and contrast images were used as input for PLS, providing group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, resting-state/seed-only, between-group-only, outside age range, or non-empirical) are violated. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of interactive joint-action (leading vs following) that probes social cognitive processes (mentalizing, perception of others) during a social task. Participants are healthy adults (n=18, mean ages ~40) within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Leading>Following, Following>Leading, conjunctions) with Talairach coordinates and figures, and whole-brain regression analyses; results are presented for the healthy participant group. Therefore it meets all listed inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

The study uses task-based fMRI of social perception (trustworthiness/fear appraisal) and includes a healthy adult control group; however, the paper does not clearly report a whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map explicitly identified for the healthy/control group alone. The reported whole-brain analyses appear to be across all participants or focus on group contrasts (BPD vs controls) and ROI analyses for the amygdala are reported for controls. Inclusion criterion I5 requires a clear, group-level whole-brain healthy/control task map; that requirement is not met. Therefore the study must be excluded under E4 (reporting only between-group contrasts or pooled analyses without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

This is an fMRI study of social processing (real-time mutual eye contact) in healthy adults. The task is explicitly social (mutual gaze/eye-blink entrainment) and uses functional MRI (hyperscanning fMRI) with task conditions (LIVE vs REPLAY). The sample is healthy adults (final analyzed N=30 participants; mean age ~21.7 years), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (LIVE > REPLAY) with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinates, and describes whole-brain interbrain synchronization and GLM results in the text/tables/figures. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a socioemotional Face Processing Task (fearful vs neutral faces) during functional MRI, addressing social-related processing (I3). The sample comprises 49 healthy adult participants (ages 18–33) with results reported for this healthy group (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (F > N, N > F) using whole-brain TFCE/FWE-corrected analyses, including coordinates, figures, and descriptions in the text (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are violated. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (cyberball) probing social exclusion/affiliation processes in healthy adult participants (female, mean age ~21.7). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses with voxelwise thresholds and coordinates (including clusters surviving FWE small-volume correction) and provides coordinate tables and described contrasts for the healthy/control sample. All required inclusion criteria for fMRI task activation in healthy adults are met, and no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social perception (visual processing of dyadic interactions), using healthy adult participants (N=21, ages 18–35). The authors performed whole-brain preprocessing and GLM estimation to generate run-wise whole-brain beta maps and report group-level statistical analyses (one-sample t-tests) and whole-brain searchlight analyses. Results include group-level voxelwise classification/searchlight findings and discussion of whole-brain effects. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for: I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task analyses/maps), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or resting-state-only) apply.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (N=31, ages 18–35) using a social-perception task (gender judgments while viewing faces differing by facial disfigurement) that probes social-related processing (perception/understanding of others, stigma/dehumanization). The authors performed whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SnPM nonparametric whole-brain contrasts, cluster-level FWE correction) and report significant whole-brain activations and deactivations for the healthy sample (figures/tables and ROI/item-wise follow-ups are provided). Thus the paper meets the fMRI social-processing objective, includes a healthy adult sample, and reports unmasked group-level whole-brain task activation maps. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study uses task-based fMRI during a social neuroeconomic task (prisoners' dilemma) probing social behaviour and cognition. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=15; ages 18–50) reported separately. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses for the control group (one-sample t-tests and per-group analyses with whole-brain results described and visualized; thresholding and cluster reporting are provided), satisfying the requirement for unmasked healthy-group whole-brain activation maps. Constructs assessed (trust/cooperation, mentalizing, face trustworthiness) fall within social-related processing. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, or missing healthy-group whole-brain maps) apply. Therefore the study meets all relevant inclusion criteria for this review.

The study uses task-based fMRI of social processing (dynamic facial expressions) and includes a healthy adult control group, so I3 and I4 are satisfied. However, the paper does not report an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map clearly identified for the healthy/control group (TD). The reported whole-brain analyses focus on between-group comparisons and found no significant additional activations; the main task results are given as ROI/MANCOVA analyses and DCM (effective connectivity). Therefore it fails the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map (I5) and thus meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

This paper reports task-based functional MRI of action observation and weight-discrimination tasks probing perception/understanding of others (social perception). Healthy adult participants are included (multiple experiments with n=79 healthy participants; controls for the SCA6 patient study are reported separately), and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and contrasts (ActionOBS–CtrlOBS; Sleeve/NoSleeve) are reported and described in the text, figures, and supplementary materials. Whole-brain analyses and coordinates are provided, satisfying reporting requirements. The study is empirical fMRI work in healthy adults and does not rely solely on ROI, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical methods. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=9, mean age 24) that used task-based paradigms probing social perception (selective attention to eye gaze and identity; passive viewing of direct vs averted gaze). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and statistical contrasts (face vs control; region clusters identified with z>4 and Talairach coordinates via SPM), presented in tables/figures. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present and sufficient for screening.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Inclusion I3 is satisfied: this is an fMRI study of a social task (racial ingroup/outgroup face perception). Inclusion I5 (reporting a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task map for the healthy group) cannot be confirmed from the provided text: the abstract describes amygdala BOLD differences and an ROI-based analysis but does not clearly report unmasked whole-brain voxelwise results. Inclusion I4 (healthy adult sample, ages 18–65) is not verifiable because no ages or explicit healthy adult status are reported in the excerpt. Because at least one required inclusion criterion (I5) cannot be confirmed, the study is excluded pending the full text. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be definitively applied given the incomplete text. Recommend obtaining the complete article to reassess inclusion.

The abstract indicates an fMRI study of social judgments (empathy, forgivability), so I3 (fMRI during social-related task) is satisfied. However the provided full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata), so key eligibility items cannot be verified: participant ages and health status are not reported in the supplied content (I4 not confirmable) and the paper’s reporting of whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone (I5 not confirmable). No exclusion criteria are clearly met based on available content, but because required inclusion criteria (I4 and I5) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study must be excluded pending a complete full text. Full text incomplete flag set.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of social judgment (trustworthiness of faces), meeting the review objective. It tests perception/understanding of others using an explicit/implicit trustworthiness task and reports behavioral and neuroimaging results. Sample: healthy adult participants (final N=14, ages 18–30) with group-level random-effects analyses. Whole-brain voxelwise statistical parametric maps and group contrasts (main effect of trustworthiness, task effects, interactions) are reported with coordinate tables and figures; small-volume corrections are applied for ROIs but whole-brain/unmasked results and thresholds are described. The full article text including Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study of social-cognitive attribution (perception/understanding of self and others) using task-based fMRI. Participants: 12 healthy adults (ages 20–51). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses (fixed-effects, voxelwise thresholding, tables of coordinates and figures) for contrasts of interest (internal vs external attributions; self-serving vs non-self-serving), with results presented in tables/figures. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, reports healthy-group whole-brain task effects, participants within age range, empirical study with original fMRI data). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, tables/figures described).

This is an fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults using a social-interactive task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) to manipulate perceived cooperativeness and intentionality. The scanned sample comprises healthy adult participants (mean age 25.6, range 21–36). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with contrasts and tables of peak coordinates and discusses activations in a priori ROIs and whole-brain results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (subjects, paradigm, image acquisition/analysis), Results (behavioral and neuroimaging, tables/figures), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis eligibility for inclusion as an fMRI whole-brain study of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This study reports a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adult humans (N=13, mean age 27.2) in which subjects passively viewed realistic video clips of social interactions (social-related processing). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (ANOVA, voxelwise P ≤ 0.05 corrected) with figures and a table of activated clusters for contrasts (relational vs. alone; relational vs. rest), clearly from the healthy/control group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social gaze processing (mutual vs. averted gaze) in healthy adult participants. The methods report task-based BOLD fMRI, behavioral validation, and both ROI and voxelwise (whole-brain) group-level analyses, including group-averaged t-statistic activation maps displayed on a standard brain. The sample comprises healthy young adults (reported as ‘healthy young adults’), meeting the healthy adult sample criterion. Whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps are explicitly described and visualized, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, and empirical with original fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it reports an fMRI task probing social processing (cooperation vs. competition) with healthy adult participants (ages 21–28). The full text includes methods, participant info, task design, and group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical contrasts (e.g., cooperation vs. independent; competition vs. independent), with thresholding and tables/figures described. Whole-brain results are reported and described for the healthy sample. The article is an empirical fMRI study (NeuroImage 2004) with complete core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical paper). Therefore I include this study for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (evaluative judgments of guilt and embarrassment), with healthy adult participants (N=19, ages within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts (G−N, E−N) using random-effects analyses, tables of coordinates, figures, and thresholding procedures. All required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

Full text provided is incomplete (only abstract and metadata). While the abstract indicates fMRI experiments addressing theory-of-mind/social interaction (satisfying I3), the paper lacks accessible methods, participant details, and whole-brain result reporting needed to confirm eligibility. I cannot verify that a healthy adult sample (I4) was used, nor that at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from the healthy/control group is reported (I5/I6). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met from the available content, but inability to confirm required inclusion criteria and the incomplete full text necessitate exclusion at this stage. Recommend obtaining the full article (PDF) to reassess.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI to investigate a social-related construct (perception/understanding of self via self-face recognition), includes healthy adult participants (n=10, mean age 26.9, ages within 18–65), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (self>other and other>self) with cluster-thresholding and coordinates in tables/figures. The full text contains methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age sample, or non-empirical paper).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (impression formation) in healthy adults (n=14, ages 18.3–23.7), using task-based fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., person-impression > other trial types; impression > sequencing) with statistical thresholds (P<0.001) and MNI coordinates/tables and figures, clearly from the healthy control group. Core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This paper reports an event-related BOLD fMRI study of self-face versus familiar and unfamiliar faces, which directly addresses social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Self). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=12; mean age ~19), and results are presented as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM contrasts: unknown vs scrambled, familiar vs unknown, self vs familiar) with tables and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range age, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=15, mean age 24.4) that investigates processing of angry prosody—a social-communication/emotion task—meeting the review objective. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses and voxelwise contrasts with MNI coordinates (e.g., STS, amygdala, OFC), clearly identified as healthy/control group results. Full article text including methods, results, and discussion is provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This is an fMRI study using a social cognition task (theory of mind and empathy cartoons) in healthy adult participants (n=13; ages 19–36). The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses (SPM2) with reported thresholding and tables/figures of activation foci and conjunction/contrast results, clearly from the healthy/control group. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating social-related processing (gaze, social communication, perception of self/others) using virtual characters. Participants were healthy adults (n=18, mean age 25.9; analyses reported for n=17), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with contrasts, coordinate tables, SPM maps, ROI masking reported but not limited to ROIs. Whole-brain results are clearly described (MNI/Talairach coordinates, statistical thresholds). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult volunteers (age 20–28) that explicitly examines perception/understanding of self vs other (detection of visual feedback ownership), which falls under social-related constructs. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Aa–As, Pa–Ps) with cluster- and voxel-level thresholds and coordinates (tables/figures), analyzed with SPM2, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full article text including introduction, methods, results, and discussion is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within 18–65, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (spontaneous retrieval of affective person knowledge during face perception) in healthy adult participants (ages 18–32). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with statistically thresholded contrasts and Talairach coordinates (Tables and coordinates provided for group contrasts), fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. The sample consists of healthy adults and results are reported for the healthy group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, or non-empirical restrictions). Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

Full text appears incomplete (only summary/abstract and metadata provided). Inclusion I3 (fMRI during social-related task: face perception) is satisfied based on the summary. However key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed: I4 (participant sample details/healthy adults 18–65) not reported in provided content, and I5 (reporting of at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map for healthy group) cannot be verified from the summary alone. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are explicitly met based on the available content; the study appears empirical. Because the provided full text is incomplete and critical criteria cannot be verified, the study is excluded pending complete full text.

This fMRI study used an interactive social task provoking reactive aggression (social interaction, perception/understanding of others, empathy). Participants were healthy adult males (mean age 28.6, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with random-effects t-statistics, thresholding, and MNI coordinates (tables/figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-state-only; reports healthy-group whole-brain task effects).

This is an fMRI study of social cognition: participants viewed photographs of social groups and made affective/social judgments (SCM emotions), satisfying the social-related task requirement. Participants were healthy adults (Princeton undergraduates; mean age 19.5; Study 1: n=10; Study 2: n=12), meeting the sample inclusion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects GLM, Talairach normalization), with coordinates, t-values, and contrast maps (e.g., subtractive analyses and 3-versus-1 contrasts) for the healthy participant group. Results are reported as whole-brain group effects in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and participants are within 18–65). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that directly investigates social-related processing (judgments of social concepts). It reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps and voxelwise contrasts (categorical subtractions and conjunction analyses) with coordinates and thresholding described, and results are clearly attributable to the healthy participant group (n=26, mean age 29.4). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (subjects, fMRI paradigm, image acquisition, analysis), Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results), and I6 (results reported with coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete for core content.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of social perception (facial emotion recognition vs age judgment), meeting the social-related task requirement. Sample comprises 29 healthy adult participants (ages 20–35), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and contrasts (FWE-corrected thresholds), with tables of coordinates and figures showing group activation maps for the healthy sample (explicit and implicit conditions), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

The study is an empirical fMRI experiment targeting social cognition (self-referential processing and perspective taking), satisfying I3. Participants are described as a healthy sample (no clinical groups reported), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level activations in specific MPFC regions (ventral/dorsal anterior MPFC, posterior dorsal MPFC, left dorsal MPFC), which indicates whole-brain task-evoked group effects consistent with I5 and the acceptable reporting formats in I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. However, the provided content appears to be an abstract-like excerpt rather than the full article (methods, full participant demographics, and full statistical reporting are not included), so fulltext_incomplete=true and certainty is moderate. Inclusion is recommended but verification against the full article (to confirm participant ages and explicit whole-brain voxelwise maps/thresholding) is advised.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (communicative speech production) in healthy adult participants (N=29, ages 18–24). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses and task contrasts (communication vs description; familiar vs unfamiliar) with statistical thresholds and cluster correction, and provides tables/figures of activated regions. This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (perception of others' actions/biological motion), with a healthy adult sample (13 right-handed males, mean age 28.2). The study used task-based fMRI while participants viewed others in pain (a social cognition task related to perception/understanding of others), recruited healthy adult participants (N≈36, ages ~21), and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps and coordinates (whole-brain analyses with FDR correction, tables/figures). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing verification of methods and whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and it is an empirical fMRI study). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included in the review.

This paper reports original fMRI data using social/person-related tasks (familiar, famous, and novel faces; social closeness judgments) addressing perception and understanding of others. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=15 analyzed, mean age 22.33), within the 18–65 range. The authors report group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (random-effects GLM; voxelwise FDR-corrected maps and cluster-thresholded results) and provide peak coordinates in Talairach space. Whole-brain contrasts relevant to social processing are clearly described (e.g., Facesfamous vs. Facesnovel; Facesfriends vs. Facesnovel), and results are reported in tables and figures. No exclusion criteria appear to be met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical design). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This study used task-based fMRI to investigate perception of face gender (a social-perception construct: perception/understanding of others). Participants were healthy adults (ages 19–42; N=16, one excluded for motion). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (random-effects GLM, contrast gender-different > gender-same) with cluster-corrected statistical maps and coordinates (Figure and Talairach coordinates). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (final N=17; mean age 23.5) using a social-related task contrasting human vs computer opponents (social resource conflict), satisfying the review topic. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8, second-level random-effects factorial models), thresholded maps, figures, and tables of activation coordinates for contrasts such as Conflict > No-Conflict and interaction effects, clearly derived from the healthy participant group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=24, ages 18–27) that used task-based paradigms probing social-cognitive processing (Why-How action identification and Categories-Exemplars), i.e., social-related construal/mentalizing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests; thresholds and cluster correction via Monte Carlo; tables/figures of activations) for relevant contrasts and conjunctions. Whole-brain results are described in text, tables and figures. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study that examines social perception (comparisons of physical attractiveness of people) using a task involving judgments about others’ beauty—a social-related construct (I3). Sample comprises 25 healthy adult women (mean age 23.46), meeting the healthy adult age/sample requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (whole-brain thresholds, conjunctions, tables of coordinates, figures) and ROI checks, with results clearly described for the healthy participant group (I5, I6). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only samples, non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (social learning/exclusion using a cyber-ball task) in healthy adults (N=15, mean age 24.1), meeting construct and sample criteria. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results from an exploratory searchlight analysis (random-effects group analysis with family-wise error correction and MNI coordinates reported for STS), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. ROI analyses are also reported but do not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is an empirical fMRI study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (mentalizing about groups and individuals), meeting the social-related task requirement (I3). Participants are healthy adults within the 18–65 range across two experiments (N=25, ages 19–27; N=14, ages 18–23), satisfying the sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects task contrasts and multivariate searchlight results (e.g., group mental > group physical; member mental > member physical; same>different MVPA) with tables and figures of coordinates and corrected thresholds, satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no resting-state/ connectivity-only, no between-group-only contrasts, and it is empirical). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing using a real-world social task (speed-dating) with healthy adult participants (scanned N=38, ages 19–31). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Match vs Unrequited; violations of expectation) with tables of coordinates and thresholding details, and includes full Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social communication (communicative vs private intentions) in healthy adults (N=23, mean age 24). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., CInt > PInt; interaction CInt0° > CInt30°) with coordinates, figures, and statistical thresholds, and also reports psychophysiological interaction results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a social-affiliation/attachment task (hand-holding by friend, stranger, or alone) with threat/safety cues. The sample consists of healthy adults (mean age 23.6). The authors performed group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FEAT/FLAME cluster-wise thresholding) to identify ROIs and report coordinates and cluster statistics (Table 1) for threat-minus-safe contrasts and handholding interactions. Whole-brain results are clearly reported in the text/tables. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social communication (laughter perception) in healthy adults (n=18, mean age 26), using task-based paradigms manipulating social information (categorization vs. counting). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, second-level random-effects analyses with voxelwise contrasts (e.g., CSL>TIC, CAT>COU), cluster-level FWE correction, and coordinate tables/figures. Thus it satisfies I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of social communication (imitation/observation of communicative gestures) in healthy adult participants (n=20 reported; mean age 24.6), reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts with MNI coordinates and cluster-corrected statistics across multiple contrasts (e.g., IMI>CT, S>NS, interactions). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation maps reported), and I6 (coordinates/tables/figures clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets the meta-analysis objectives and all inclusion criteria. It uses functional MRI during a social-related task (compassion/empathy responses to images of human suffering; I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants aged 18–45 with analyses reported for the healthy groups (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (e.g., whole-brain Group × Redistribution Rank interaction; whole-brain corrected results identifying IPC and DLPFC clusters), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5). Whole-brain results are described in the text and supplemental materials (coordinates and corrected clusters), which meets I6. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROI-only analyses, nor restricted to connectivity/resting-state only, nor to participants outside the age range, and this is an empirical fMRI study. Full text appears complete for screening (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating social-related processing (playing for self, friend, antagonist) in healthy adults (N=31, ages 18–26). It reports whole-brain, group-level task activation analyses (repeated-measures ANOVAs) with voxelwise results, coordinate tables, and figures; small-volume corrections are applied but whole-brain maps and coordinates are presented. Full methods, results, and discussion are included in the provided full text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI social processing in healthy adults and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating neural responses during a social communication task (message propagation), satisfying the social-related task requirement. Participants were healthy adults (interns N=19, producers N=79; mean ages ~20.5), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (whole-brain thresholding, corrected p-values, MNI coordinates reported in tables/figures) rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only results. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met, and no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study that directly investigates perception/understanding of others’ action ‘vitality forms’ (a social-related construct) using a task contrasting attention to action goal (what) vs vitality (how). Participants are healthy adults (n=19, ages ~21–29). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (e.g., contrasts how vs what) with reported coordinates, statistical thresholds (PFWE), tables and figures. Whole-brain results for the healthy/control group are clearly described. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

The study reports an fMRI experiment examining social cognition (theory of mind, emotion and pain judgments about others) using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=46 females, ages 18–31). It includes group-level, whole-brain second-level analyses (one-sample t-tests with whole-brain maps, tables, and figures) and multivoxel pattern analyses reported across the whole brain. Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, figures, and tables. All inclusion criteria are met (I3: task-based fMRI of social processes; I4: healthy adult sample within 18–65; I5: group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported; I6: whole-brain results provided in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-evaluation task (being watched by a peer) during fMRI, reporting task-evoked activations and connectivity. The sample includes healthy adult participants (ages 8.0–22.9, thus containing adults 18–22.9 within the 18–65 range). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise statistical results (corrected clusters and peak coordinates for MPFC and striatal coupling) and provides coordinates and cluster statistics in the text/supplement. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided full text.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception: participants viewed dyadic nonverbal interactions and rated naturalness during task-based fMRI. Sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=21, ages 23–33). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (multiple contrasts, cluster-level corrected; coordinates and tables/figures provided). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and is empirical). Full text is present (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social impression formation (social perception/understanding of others) using task-based BOLD fMRI (I3). Sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=19, mean age 19.1) within 18–65 (I4). The manuscript reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts from the healthy sample (e.g., functional localizer contrast form impression > sequencing; cluster-corrected results and Talairach coordinates presented in tables and text), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements (I5, I6). Analyses include cluster-corrected maps and coordinates (Tables 1–2) and describe methods for whole-brain GLM and corrections. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range-sample, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates social perception (biological motion) using a passive viewing task—satisfying I3. The sample includes a clearly reported healthy adult group (n=48; ages 20–35) with results reported separately—satisfying I4. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts are reported for adults (e.g., biological > scrambled motion, Sex × Condition ANOVA) with thresholding, cluster correction, tables of coordinates, and figures—satisfying I5 and I6. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply: the paper does not report only ROI or only connectivity or only between-group contrasts, includes adults within 18–65, and is empirical. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=45, ages 19–28) that uses task-based fMRI to investigate social-signal detection and mental-state inference. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests, voxel-by-voxel regression, cluster correction) with coordinates/figures and tables of activations. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, tasks, fMRI acquisition/preprocessing, analyses), Results and Discussion. All inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (third-party punishment; mentalizing/attribution of others’ intentions), conducted in healthy adult participants (N=26, ages mean 26 within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects multisubject GLM; whole-brain FDR thresholding) and provides peak coordinates and figures describing activations (e.g., R TPJ interaction, R anterior insula main effect). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I3, I4, I5, I6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using social stimuli (traffic campaign videos) to probe socio-cognitive processing (STS responses), with healthy adult participants aged 19–30. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (CV vs NV) for each group (Fig. 1) and describes between- and within-group analyses; whole-brain results for the healthy control/safe driver group are clearly presented. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of face processing (a social-perception construct) using a simple viewing task (faces vs objects), satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample includes a healthy adult group (N=21, ages 18–37) reported separately in participant tables and ROI statistics. The manuscript performs and reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (faces>objects) with results presented in figures and Table 3 (coordinates) and whole-brain maps (regression and contrasts), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Whole-brain results are described in the text and tables (acceptable per I6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related attribute framing task (self and reflected perspectives) in healthy adults (N=21, ages 19–41). The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (GLM contrasts such as positive minus negative frame, frame-inconsistent minus frame-consistent) with thresholding and peak coordinates described in the Results, satisfying whole-brain group-level reporting. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata/references provided). The abstract shows an fMRI social task evaluating approachability of faces, so inclusion criterion I3 (social-related fMRI task) is met. However, I cannot confirm participant ages and that the reported results are from a healthy adult group (I4) because the full methods/participant section is missing, nor can I verify that the paper reports a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map for the healthy group (I5/I6). Although the abstract describes activations (e.g., left amygdala) and references SPM and cluster thresholds, without the full text I cannot confirm whole-brain, voxelwise group maps or tabled coordinates. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met from the available content. Because required inclusion criteria (I4 and I5) cannot be confirmed from the provided incomplete full text, I exclude the study pending access to the full article.

This article reports task-based fMRI studies of social/empathic processing (emotional egocentricity bias) in healthy adult participants, with group-level voxelwise analyses and reported coordinates/tables. Specifically: (1) uses fMRI during a social-related task (empathic judgments; fulfils I3); (2) samples are healthy adult participants (female undergraduates; fulfils I4); (3) reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical contrasts (exploratory whole-brain analysis in fMRI Experiment 1 and group-level contrasts with reported MNI coordinates in fMRI Experiment 2; fulfils I5); (4) results are reported as coordinates/tables and described in text (fulfils I6). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates social-related processing using a task (Dynamic Social Gesture) involving social vs. nonsocial gestures, actor-orientation, and face-visibility. The sample is a healthy young adult group (N=20; mean age 21.41, range 16.9–25.7) and the paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (TFCE with permutation testing) with tables/figures of results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI social-task studies with healthy adults and provides whole-brain activation maps/reports.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=32, mean age ~24.7), using a social incentive force task manipulating collaboration, competition, and individual contexts. The study collected task-evoked BOLD data and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM random-effects; clusterwise FWE correction) with figures and a table of activation peaks (ventral basal ganglia, TPJ, mPFC, etc.). Behavioral and structural (VBM) results are also reported. All required inclusion criteria are met: I3 (functional MRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, age within range, and empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete, containing introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study directly probes social-related processing (judgments of social coordination) in healthy adult participants (N=20, ages 23–39). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects task activation analyses are reported (FDR-corrected), with tables and figures describing voxelwise results and coordinate tables. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry) study relating grey matter volumes to proneness to moral sentiments using a behavioral task (VMST). It does not report any task-evoked functional MRI whole-brain results from the healthy group. A subgroup (N=29) had prior fMRI data referenced for secondary correlational analyses, but the paper does not present a healthy-group, whole-brain, task-evoked fMRI statistical map required by the review. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3 (study uses fMRI during a social-related task) and I5 (reports at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group). The sample meets I4 (healthy adult participants). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study reports fMRI during a social-related task (live verbal communication) in healthy adults (22 right-handed women, mean age ~27), with group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (talking, listening, imagining) and inter-individual coupling analyses. Whole-brain results are reported with cluster thresholds, figures, and supplementary tables/coordinates. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group voxelwise task maps reported), and I6 (results presented in figures/tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, age range appropriate, empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete.

The article reports an fMRI task explicitly probing social judgments (trustworthiness, attractiveness, happiness) using vocal stimuli in a sample of healthy adults (N=44; ages 21–60), satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement (I4). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-level FWE correction and MNI coordinates (conjunctions, contrasts, tables/figures), providing whole-brain task activation maps and coordinate tables (I5,I6). The task is clearly social-related (I3). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

Study is an empirical fMRI investigation of social communication/empathy using naturalistic video stimuli (meets I3). Sample comprises 27 healthy adult participants (mean age 34.07), meeting the healthy adult sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM contrasts and provides coordinate tables/figures of task-evoked activations (satisfies I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only, no resting-state/only-connectivity-only analyses, no between-group-only contrasts, age within range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI task study of social processing (empathy, Theory of Mind, self–other differentiation) in healthy adult participants (n=15, ages 21–40). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (ANOVA, contrasts), thresholding procedures, cluster extents, coordinates, conjunctions, and figures/tables of activations—i.e., voxelwise whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy group. Core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), and I6 (results presented in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This is an fMRI study of a social task (one-shot Prisoner’s Dilemma) in healthy adult participants (N=35 after losses; mean age 24.6), reporting group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (contrasts and cluster-corrected results) with coordinates and figures. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided. The paper is empirical, not ROI-only, and reports whole-brain GLM contrasts clearly from the healthy sample. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This publication is a narrative review article (non-empirical) in Japanese and does not report original fMRI data, participant samples, methods, or group-level whole-brain task activation maps for healthy adults. Exclusion E6 (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data) applies. No inclusion criteria are met: I3 (fMRI during a social task) not met, I4 (healthy adult sample reported) not met, I5 (whole-brain group-level maps reported) not met. Full text appears to be only abstract/metadata, so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This paper reports an fMRI task examining perception/processing of personally familiar faces (partner, child, friend), a social cognition/affiliation-related paradigm relevant to perception and understanding of others (meets I3). It includes a separate healthy control group (13 healthy adults; mean age 64.5 ±5.7) reported separately from the patient (meets I4). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts from the control group (e.g., partner > unfamiliar; whole-brain FWE-corrected results and tables/figures), satisfying I5 and I6. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and is complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Note: controls are older adults near the upper age bound (mean 64.5) but are a healthy adult group reported separately; therefore included.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the ultimatum game (a social decision-making task) and reports task-evoked whole-brain voxelwise contrasts. It includes a healthy adult group (n=15, ages 19–28) with group-level one-sample t-tests and between-group analyses; results are reported as whole-brain maps and coordinates. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social interaction (free online reciprocal imitation) in healthy adults (N=23 females, ages 18–30). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., imitating vs rest, being imitated vs rest, observation vs rest) with multiple-comparison correction (FWE), and provides coordinates/tables and figures. It therefore satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age appropriate, and empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This study used task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=8, ages 22–39) receiving natural interpersonal touch, a social-related stimulus. It reports group-level whole-brain spatial maps (group ICA z-maps thresholded and displayed across the brain) together with task-evoked component time courses and statistical comparisons between stimulus types. Thus it meets inclusion: I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), and I5 (group-level whole-brain maps/task-evoked responses). Reporting format is acceptable per I6. The paper is not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state-only analyses without task maps, and not a non-empirical paper. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore I include this study for the review.

This empirical paper reports fMRI data from a faces-versus-houses task in a sample of healthy young adults (mean age 18.87; fMRI subset N=22 after exclusions). The study conducted standard first- and second-level SPM analyses and reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activations (significant clusters and a Table 2; figures show FWE-corrected activations). Face perception is a social-related construct (perception/understanding of others). Healthy adult results are reported separately (the control/non-clinical sample), satisfying the sample requirement. Therefore the paper meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

Included: The study reports task-based fMRI during social-related trials (social distance: friends vs acquaintances), satisfying the social processing requirement. The sample is healthy adults (N=15; ages 20–28), meeting the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain searchlight and RSA analyses with group statistical maps/clusters and tables (conjunction analyses, FDR-corrected clusters) described in the text and tables, satisfying the whole-brain reporting requirement. Reporting of whole-brain results is explicit (clusters, maps, tables). No exclusion criteria are met: this is not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes an explicit healthy-group task effect, and is an empirical fMRI study. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used task-based fMRI of social processing (social closeness judgments) in a sample that includes healthy adults (ages 19–30), satisfying inclusion criteria I3 and I4. However, the fMRI results are analyzed and reported using ROI-based extractions (mean beta weights from predefined anatomical ROIs) rather than reporting any unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation maps for the healthy group. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) and fails to meet inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise map). Full text appears complete. Decision: EXCLUDE.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (self/other/reflected evaluations), includes a healthy adult group (N=19; ages 22–31), and reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps and cluster results (voxelwise thresholds, AlphaSim correction, tables/figures). Whole-brain analyses and coordinates for effects are provided and results for the healthy adult group are clearly described. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social-related paradigm (bystander/emergency observation) using healthy adult participants (aged 18–27). The methods describe whole-brain, group-level random-effects GLM analyses and report voxelwise results (parametric effects and contrasts) with cluster-level corrections and tables/figures of activation, meeting whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognitive processing (causal attribution/mentalizing) in a healthy adult sample (N=20, ages 18–41). The task is social (self/other/situation attributions). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and whole-brain FWE-corrected results (conjunctions and contrasts versus a truth baseline) and refers to Table 1 and figures with coordinates; whole-brain ANOVA and contrasts are described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=50, ages 18–49) investigating social attribution (rating another’s awareness). This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants performed an impression-formation task (social evaluation of others varying in moral and financial status) during task-based fMRI. The study reports task-based fMRI during a social-related paradigm (empathy induction via traffic-awareness campaign videos), includes a healthy adult sample (20 males, ages 20–28), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (CV > NV) with FWE-corrected results summarized in tables/figures. This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (25 scanned; ages within 18–65) that uses task-based fMRI during a social economic interaction (repeated public good game) addressing social tie formation (affiliation/attachment and understanding others). This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (mutual understanding) using a task that requires communicative interaction between participants.
