This full text meets all inclusion criteria. I3: The study uses task-based fMRI to examine prosocial learning and empathy (social-related processing). I4: Sample comprises healthy adult participants aged 19–32 (n=31; healthy males). I5: The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps/main effects (reports main effects at P < 0.05 FWE whole-brain and presents conjunction and contrast results; supplementary tables/figures show whole-brain activation and coordinates). I6: Whole-brain results are provided as coordinates, statistical maps, and described in the text and supplementary material. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not outside age range, empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplemental references). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an original empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that investigates social-related processes (mentalizing, empathy, prosocial behavior). It reports task-based fMRI using whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM12; cluster-level correction with voxelwise threshold p<0.001) and presents group-level contrasts and tables of activation (e.g., Mentalizing Dissimilar>Similar clusters, Empathy Painful>Non-Painful), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=32; mean age 22.7), within the 18–65 range. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and References. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps and coordinate tables. Inclusion criteria met: I3 — task-based fMRI probing social processing (mentalizing about friends vs kin); I4 — healthy adult sample (n=25 females, mean age 23.2 within 18–65); I5 — reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (GLM, cluster-thresholded maps, tables of clusters/coordinates); I6 — whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures and described in the text. No exclusion criteria are triggered: results are not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not limited to subgroup-only comparisons, participants are within the eligible age range, and this is an empirical fMRI paper with original data. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study uses a Face Matching Task (implicit emotional face processing) which is a social-related task (perception/understanding of others). The sample comprises a healthy adult group (n=10, mean age 25, within 18–65) and results for the healthy group are reported. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain GLM task-evoked analyses (one-sample t-tests; contrasts like face processing and fear>neutral) with coordinates and figures (Table S2, Figures S1–S3), satisfying whole-brain reporting; whole-brain results are described in the text and supplementary materials. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion, conclusions) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not only resting-state/seed connectivity, not only between-group contrasts, ages within range, empirical data present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (social competition) with a task manipulating social context, meeting I3. Participants are healthy adults (20 females aged 18–35), meeting I4. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation contrasts and cluster-corrected results with peak coordinates (whole-brain analyses, Competition>No Competition, working memory and feedback contrasts), satisfying I5 and I6. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion.

The study reports an fMRI task probing social communication/mentalizing (social-related processing), with analyses linking neural activity to social-language stimuli and re-transmission. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=19, mean age 20.55). The paper reports whole-brain task-evoked results (parametric whole-brain searches for social language in/out, thresholded and reported with figures/tables), satisfying the requirement for group-level whole-brain maps from the healthy group. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and is complete for screening. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (emotion recognition and gaze integration), involving healthy adult participants and reporting group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses. The task probes perception/understanding of others (social communication/mentalizing). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise results (PLS analyses) with tables of peak coordinates and figures for the healthy age groups. Although one group includes older adults (65–75) outside the 18–65 range, the younger group (17–27) contains adults within the 18–65 window and is reported separately, satisfying the sample criterion. The manuscript contains complete core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) and presents whole-brain healthy-group effects rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social processing (empathy for pain) using a task explicitly probing perception/understanding of others’ pain (I3). The sample comprises healthy adult male participants aged 18–40 with group sizes reported and analyses on healthy participants (I4). The paper provides whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results (INJECTION>QTIP, BIOPSY>QTIP), including family-wise error corrected whole-brain analyses, figures, and coordinate tables (I5, I6). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only reporting, no resting-state/seed-only analyses, no exclusively between-group-only unmasked omission, and participants are within age range). Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (attribution of emotions/theory-of-mind) using tasks that explicitly manipulate emotion vs expression and passive viewing of human and non-human faces, satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample consists of healthy adults (initial N=18; analyzed N=16–17; ages 21–46), meeting the age and health criteria. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (e.g., Emotion > Expression and Face > Scramble contrasts, conjunctions, cluster-level FWE-corrected maps, and whole-brain results in figures/tables), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement; results are described in text and figures. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state only, between-group-only contrasts, non-eligible age groups only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (perception of emotional facial expressions, including affiliation-relevant emotions) in a sample of 40 healthy volunteers, fulfilling I3 and I4. The abstract describes group-level neural responses in multiple brain regions (thalamus, temporo-parietal regions, cerebellum, amygdala, cortical areas), indicating whole-brain task-evoked results consistent with I5 and acceptable reporting formats per I6. However, the provided full text appears incomplete (mainly abstract/highlights/metadata), so detailed methods (exact ages, analytic scope) cannot be fully verified. Therefore inclusion is recommended but with moderate confidence pending confirmation from the complete full text.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (faces/emotion) in healthy adults. Participants were healthy adults aged 21–33 (final N=25). The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses (random-effects faces>objects localizer and whole-brain searchlight decoding of task and valence, with corrected and uncorrected thresholds; Table 3 and figures report whole-brain results). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social interaction recognition (task: discriminating interacting vs non-interacting point-light displays), includes a healthy adult group (ages 20–41) reported separately, and reports group-level whole-brain task activation results (SI > NM contrasts) using standard second-level SPM analyses with cluster/FWE-corrected results. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study uses task-based fMRI that probes social-related processes (sharing, mentalizing, self-related processing) while participants read and consider sharing news articles. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (ages 18–24) and is reported separately for the healthy groups. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (see SI: whole-brain searches, Fig. S3 and Table S5) with voxelwise correction procedures described, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group maps. Results and methods are presented in full (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and SI). Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social/person knowledge retrieval using healthy adult participants. The paper reports task-based fMRI during social-related tasks (retrieval of biographical/person attributes such as status and personality traits), meeting I3. Samples are healthy adults in the 18–65 range (study 1: n=24, Mage=23.21; study 2: n=26, Mage=20.38), meeting I4. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts (e.g., all memory > baseline; status memory > baseline; trait memory > baseline) thresholded at voxel-level FWE P<0.05 and provides coordinates/tables/figures, meeting I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within age range, and this is an empirical paper with original fMRI data. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mentalising/theory-of-mind) in healthy adults. The fMRI task is explicitly social (mentalising vs factual memory), meeting I3. The sample includes a healthy adult group (fMRI N=17, mean age 22 ±2.9), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., mentalising > factual; parametric modulation), thresholding and tables of coordinates (Table 1) and visualization of whole-brain maps, meeting I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, open-access fMRI study using a social task (pseudo-interactive joke task) that probes social action-outcome contingency (social interaction, self/other processing). The sample is 38 healthy adults (age 19–29). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps and thresholded SPM results (FWE-corrected cluster results, tables of peak coordinates, and figures) for multiple within-subject contrasts (SELF vs OTHER, listener responses, interaction/contingency effects). Although PPI connectivity analyses are included, the study also provides unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This empirical fMRI study examines social-related processing (decisions to share information, perspective-taking) during a task involving considering sharing/selecting news articles, satisfying I3. Sample comprises healthy adults aged 18–24 (N=41 analyzed), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation contrasts (select > content, share > content, share > select) with corrected thresholds and references to Table 2 and Figure 4, satisfying I5 and acceptable reporting per I6. ROI analyses are present but whole-brain results are explicitly reported; no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and paper is empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext is complete.

The article reports an empirical fMRI study of social decision-making in healthy adults. Neuroimaging methods: fMRI data were acquired (3T scanners), GLM and random-effects group analyses were performed, whole-brain statistical maps were reported (thresholded p<.001 with SnPM correction) and results/localizations (dACC, dlPFC, parietal, insula, etc.) are described; maps are available on NeuroVault. Participants: a neuroimaging cohort of healthy adults (n=72 initial, final n=62) aged 18–53, satisfying the 18–65 criterion. The task is explicitly social (manipulation of visibility of other participants’ locations/points) and examines social influence integration. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participant ages in range, empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social decision-making paradigm (Trust Game), satisfying the social-related task requirement. Participants are healthy adults aged 18–30 (n=19 included in imaging analyses), meeting the sample criterion. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (GLM contrasts with cluster correction) and reports brain activation results in tables/figures (univariate activation tables and ICA network results), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. Reporting of results in tables/figures/text meets acceptable formats. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion provided.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition: participants (n=25, healthy adults aged 18–27) performed mental simulations of 20 personally familiar people across contexts during whole-brain fMRI acquisition. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain searchlight MVPA and random-effects t tests with permutation-based correction and presents whole-brain maps/tables (Figures, Table 1). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked results), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, nor non-empirical). Full text is complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-emotional processing (schadenfreude and fremdscham), using a task that explicitly involves perception/understanding of others’ social situations. Sample: N=34 healthy adult males (ages 19–31), reported separately by group; thus a healthy adult group is analyzed. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (SIT vs NEUT) with voxelwise FWE-corrected results and tables/figures, clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Whole-brain results are reported (not limited to ROI-only), and connectivity analyses are additional but do not replace whole-brain task effects. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (theory-of-mind/implicit belief processing) in healthy adults (mean age 24.4; final N=22). The paper reports a group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM contrast from the explicit general-belief localizer (false-belief vs false-photograph) used to define ROIs (q(FDR)<0.05), which constitutes a task-evoked whole-brain statistical map for the healthy sample. The task is clearly social-related (perception/understanding of others). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided, and healthy-group results are reported separately. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is excluded because it meets exclusion criterion E2 (reports only ROI-based MVPA analyses with no group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation map reported for the healthy adult group). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses task fMRI of social cognition/theory-of-mind) and I4 (healthy adult sample, ages within 18–65). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly reported group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map from the healthy/control group). Although the paper uses individual-subject localizers (first-level Belief>Photo contrasts) and ROI definitions and reports ROI-based MVPA and classification results, I find no group-level whole-brain activation maps, coordinate tables, or unmasked healthy-group voxelwise contrasts described in the main text or supplementary materials provided here. Therefore it fails I5 and falls under E2.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of social/affiliative processing: participants viewed romantic, sexual, and neutral images to probe affiliation/romantic processing (meets I3). Sample consists of 20 healthy adult men aged 22–50, reported and analyzed separately by group (monogamous vs non-monogamous), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion (I4). The authors performed whole-brain, voxelwise analyses using FSL (FEAT) with cluster correction and report group-level task-evoked contrasts (sexual>neutral; romantic>neutral) in figures and tables, fulfilling I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria apply: this is not ROI-only (E2), not connectivity/resting-only (E3), not limited to only between-group contrasts without healthy-group task maps (E4), participants are within 18–65 (E5), and it is empirical (E6). Thus the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans (n=27, ages 20–32) examining affiliation/attachment-related processing (interest in extra-pair relationships). fMRI was acquired during task(s) with social/affiliative stimuli (IAT using monogamy/adultery images; a go/no-go task with attractive female images) and group-level whole-brain analyses are reported (IAT incongruent vs. congruent whole-brain subtraction with cluster-level FWE correction; coordinates/tables provided). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study investigating perception of social interactions (point-light walkers and animated shapes) in healthy adults (n=14, ages 20–32). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates and figures (e.g., interaction > independent; animate > physical) and describes group-constrained subject-specific fROIs. Thus it meets inclusion criteria: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in figures/coordinates). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in which participants completed an impression-formation task (forming quick impressions of Black and White faces varying in socioeconomic status), meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. The sample comprises 60 healthy adult participants (mean age 23.8), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (exploratory whole-brain regressions with voxel-wise thresholding and reported significant clusters; additional details in Supplementary Material S4), meeting whole-brain evidence requirements and the allowance for results reported in text/figures/supplementary. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group only without healthy-group map, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study reports an fMRI task explicitly probing social-related processing (perception of potential social involvement from point-light and human-like walkers), meeting the review’s topical scope (I3). The sample comprises 16 healthy adults (mean age 22.75), within the 18–65 range (I4). Group-level voxelwise task contrasts are reported at the second level with stereotaxic coordinates and thresholding (FWE-corrected), presented in tables/figures and described in the text, satisfying requirements for whole-brain task-evoked results (I5,I6). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and references, so the fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, non-empirical) are met.

The study reports only seed-based resting-state functional connectivity analyses (post-task rest FC of caudate nucleus) following listening to attachment narratives. Although it used fMRI with social/attachment stimuli and included a healthy adult sample (23 healthy males), it does not report any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked (voxelwise) activation map from the healthy/control group (no task activation contrasts; analyses are seed-based FC). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (only seed-based/resting-state connectivity reported) and does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain task-evoked map). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social/attachment-related fMRI paradigm) and I4 (healthy adult participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Full text appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication/collaboration in healthy adults (directors and matchers aged 18–33). The task involves communicative, social processing (collaborative vs. individual learning and retrieval), meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts with cluster-level correction (multiple contrasts and Table 1 listing whole-brain results) and also describes an ROI analysis, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, not between-group-only contrasts, ages within 18–65, and empirical with original fMRI data).

This is an fMRI study of social processing that meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) it uses task-based fMRI during observation of social interactions (cooperative vs affective); (I4) reports a healthy adult sample (36 right-handed adults, mean ages ~24–25); (I5) provides group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps with cluster-level correction and reported tables/figures; (I6) whole-brain results are reported in text, figures and tables (coordinates provided). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, DCM connectivity analyses, and discussion. Although the paper also reports effective connectivity (DCM), it additionally reports whole-brain activation maps, so no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore INCLUDE.

This is an empirical fMRI study of joint action (leading/following/mutual) involving direct haptic social interaction, meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. Participants are healthy adults (n=18 after exclusion), ages within 18–65, satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation contrasts (multiple whole-brain contrasts, FDR-corrected maps, and Talairach coordinates in tables/figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence; results are reported in tables and figures as acceptable. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults examining neural responses to affective vocalisations (social communication/perception). Participants: healthy adults (N=19, mean age 25.9). The task involved perception of affective vocalisations and fMRI was acquired. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (species contrast human>chimpanzee>macaque) with statistical images/coordinates (Table 2, Fig.2), clearly from the healthy sample. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI that includes a social cognition contrast (TOM vs Random) addressing social-related processing (I3); the sample comprises a large cohort of healthy adults aged 22–35 (I4); the paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps and statistics derived from HCP level-2/level-3 maps (Cohen's d and z maps), and provides cluster coordinates and figures (satisfying I5 and I6). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is present and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (self, friend, celebrity judgments) targeting self/other processing and social cognition. Sample consists of 37 healthy adult males (mean age 22.9), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects task contrasts (e.g., self vs. celebrity; friend vs. celebrity) with voxelwise statistics and coordinates (FDR-corrected), presented in tables and figures. Thus it provides whole-brain task-evoked maps from the healthy group. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity, no between-group-only contrasts, age within range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This article reports an fMRI study using a social decision-making task (modified iterated prisoner's dilemma) engaging Theory-of-Mind processes, satisfying I3. The sample comprises 20 healthy adult participants aged 23–38, satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunction analyses, COMP>COOP contrasts) with cluster-level multiple-comparison correction and tables/figures of activations, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, fMRI acquisition/preprocessing, GLM), Results (behavioral and whole-brain results), and Discussion, so core article content is present. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adults within range, and is an empirical fMRI study. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This paper reports original fMRI data directly addressing social-related processing and meets all inclusion criteria. The independent study used fMRI during a social vs. non-social image appraisal task (I3). The sample consists of healthy adults aged 23–50 with data reported for the healthy group (N=14 after one lost dataset) (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (social > non-social contrast), with thresholding and cluster results (whole-brain maps and conjunction analyses), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not limited to between-group contrasts, participants are within the age range, and the paper contains empirical fMRI data. Full text is complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study that investigates perception of others' emotions (facial and vocal prosody), which falls under social communication/perception of others (I3). Participants are healthy adults (Study 1: 25 participants aged 19–24; Study 2: 33 participants; ages within 18–65), satisfying the sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (repeated-measures ANOVA and simple effects; PFWE-corrected results and tables/figures of activations and coordinates), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, not only between-group contrasts, and participants are within the age range. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Hence include.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). The abstract indicates the study used fMRI during a social decision task, so I3 (fMRI during social-related task) is satisfied based on available information. However, the abstract does not report participants' ages (so I4 cannot be confirmed) and does not specify any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy group (I5 not verifiable). The abstract emphasizes functional connectivity results, which could reflect analyses falling under E2/E3, but this cannot be confirmed without full text. Because key inclusion criteria cannot be verified from the provided content, the study is excluded pending full-text review.

Only the abstract and metadata are provided (full text incomplete). From the abstract, the study uses task-based fMRI of social communicative prosody, so I3 is met. However key eligibility details cannot be confirmed: participant ages and whether a healthy adult group (I4) is explicitly reported, and whether group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps from the healthy/control group are reported (I5) are not verifiable from the abstract alone. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are explicitly met based on the available information. Full text is needed to determine inclusion. Therefore I exclude provisionally due to incomplete full text and inability to verify all inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (self-evaluation and endorsement of others’ evaluation) in healthy adults. Sample: healthy adult participants aged 19–24 (final N=31) meeting the age and health criteria. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts and a whole-brain multiple regression with self-esteem (thresholds and cluster-level FWE correction are provided) and tables of coordinates/figures. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion reason: E2 applies — analyses were restricted to pre-defined ROIs and the search regions were explicitly restricted to those ROIs; no unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group is reported. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (used task-based fMRI of social evaluations: intelligence and friendliness ratings from faces) and I4 (healthy adult participants, ages 18–28). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked results reported). Full text appears complete and contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

The study includes a social cognition task (social interaction vs random movement) using task-fMRI and reports group-level task activation results. Participants are healthy adults from HCP and UCLA datasets (ages reported within 21–50/22–36 ranges), meeting the age and sample requirements. The authors performed voxel-wise GLM activation analyses and present group-level whole-brain task activation results (Figures and Supplementary Figure S2 are referenced), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps), and I6 (acceptable reporting formats) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study is a double-blind, placebo-controlled fMRI experiment using a social-related task (erotic and fearful social scenes) probing affiliation/attachment and social emotion processing, satisfying the review topic. Participants: 55 healthy adult males (mean age 24.9), meeting the age/sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps and contrasts (whole-brain FWE-corrected results and contrasts such as erotic>neutral, fearful>neutral, erotic>fearful), clearly identified as coming from the healthy sample. Whole-brain results are reported in the main text (with supplementary tables/analyses), fulfilling the requirement that coordinate/whole-brain results are available. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

Study reports task-based fMRI during social-related tasks (mind perception and gaze-cueing), with a healthy adult sample (N=22; mean age 24.36, within 18–65). The paper provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (parametric regressors, cluster-based correction, peak Z and MNI coordinates, conjunction results), fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures, coordinates) is present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (mothers classifying their own child’s facial emotions—social perception/attachment), includes a healthy adult control group (CON) reported separately, and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps (FWE-corrected whole-brain results and coordinates) attributable to the control/healthy group (e.g., CON familiarity effect in medial frontal gyrus). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (recall of self- and other-related relationship episodes) in a group of healthy adult participants (N=35). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation contrasts (self-relevant > control; other > control) with FDR-corrected cluster inference and provides tables/figures of significant clusters. Although explicit participant ages are not shown in the excerpt, participants are described as healthy individuals recruited from university and community sources; the sample is reported as adults and screened for mental disorders. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age only, or non-empirical issues). Confidence is high but slightly reduced because exact age range (18–65) is not numerically listed in the provided text.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (integration of facial and vocal emotional expressions), satisfying the review’s focus on social communication and perception of others. The sample consists of healthy adults (N=24; mean age 26), meeting the age and health requirements. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (RFX) task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (e.g., conjunctions, FWE-corrected maps, tables with MNI coordinates) clearly attributed to the healthy participant group. Whole-brain results are described in text, figures, and tables. The manuscript includes independent ROI and DCM analyses but these are accompanied by whole-brain task activation results. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (trustworthiness judgments) in healthy adults. It reports task-based fMRI during a social cognition task (face-based trustworthiness judgments with feedback), includes a healthy younger adult group within the 18–65 range (20–33 years), and reports group-level voxelwise analyses including whole-brain ANOVA results (they state the ANOVA was also performed at the whole-brain level and report suprathreshold clusters, tables, and figures; Supplementary Table 2 referenced). Whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures and described in the text. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mental state prediction/understanding others) in healthy adult participants (N=28 analyzed; ages 18–22). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses: a searchlight representational similarity analysis and voxelwise repetition-suppression results with permutation TFCE correction (significant clusters in dorsal medial PFC and posterior precuneus). Methods, results, and discussion are fully present in the provided full text. Therefore inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an empirical fMRI study of social decision-making (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) in healthy adult participants (N=20, ages 21–37). It reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses (flexible factorial, one-sample t tests, cluster-level FWE-corrected maps) with tables/figures of activations. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: (I3) It uses task-based fMRI during a social interaction paradigm (iterated Prisoner's Dilemma assessing reciprocated and unreciprocated cooperation); (I4) Sample consists of healthy adult participants aged 18–22 with group-level results reported for OT vs placebo healthy groups; (I5) The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (GLM, cluster-corrected Z-thresholding) with tables/figures of significant clusters described in the text; (I6) Whole-brain results are described in the main text and presented in tables/figures. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This full-text fMRI study meets all inclusion criteria: I3 - uses functional MRI during a social task (modified Taylor Aggression Paradigm probing social provocation and decision-making); I4 - includes healthy adult participants (males aged 18–35; n=93 analyzed); I5 - reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (high > low provocation) with MNI coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction; I6 - whole-brain results are presented in tables and figures and described in the text. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E2), not limited to connectivity/resting-state (E3), include within-group healthy-group task effects rather than only between-group contrasts (E4), participants are within 18–65 (E5), and this is an empirical fMRI study with original data (not a review) (E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion provided). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI hyperscanning study of a social interactive task (pattern game) involving healthy adult participants (N=44; mean age 22.4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (GLM, FLAME) with non-parametric permutation correction and tables/figures of results (Tables 1–3, Figure 4). Thus it meets inclusion criteria: I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study examines theory of mind (a social-cognitive task) using task-based fMRI and resting-state fMRI in healthy younger and older adult groups. The abstract and highlights indicate (1) a task-based fMRI assessment of theory of mind (meets I3), (2) inclusion of healthy adult participant groups (younger and older; meets I4), and (3) use of task-defined network and intrinsic connectivity derived from task/rest data, implying group-level task activation was used to define the theory-of-mind network (likely meeting I5). The paper appears in NeuroImage and likely reports whole-brain task effects (I6 acceptable). However, only abstract/metadata were provided here (full text unavailable), so I set fulltext_incomplete=true and apply inclusion criteria provisionally. I could not directly verify the presence of explicit whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps in the available content, so inclusion is provisional pending full-text confirmation.

This is an fMRI study of face perception/recognition (social perception/understanding of others) using task-based fMRI (Experiment 1). Participants were healthy adults within the 18–65 range (Experiment 1: N=20, mean age ~25). The methods describe group-level mixed-effects (FLAME) analyses to derive group patterns of response for each condition, indicating group-level, voxelwise task-evoked maps were produced and used in subsequent analyses. Whole-brain analyses are referenced (group-level maps, registration to MNI space), and behavioral-task whole-brain results are reported/used in figures and regression analyses. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, and I5 are met; I6 (acceptable reporting formats) also applies. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (live human–human vs human–robot conversation) in healthy adults, reporting whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task: mentalizing, social motivation, social communication), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately: 21 participants, mean age 25.8), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps reported and thresholded across the whole brain; contrasts HHI vs HRI and main effects), I6 (whole-brain results are described in text and figures; data shared on NeuroVault/OpenNeuro). No exclusion criteria are met (E2–E6). Full text appears complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study reports task-based fMRI measuring social-related processing (empathy for pain/pleasure toward human and robot agents), uses a healthy adult sample (final N=26, ages 18–27), and presents whole-brain group-level random-effects analyses (cluster-corrected results, whole-brain maps and NeuroVault links). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of co-speech gesture processing within continuous narratives, addressing social communication and discourse perception (relevant to social-related processing). The sample comprises 20 healthy adult participants (ages 22–35). Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses were performed and reported (SPM12; contrasts, cluster thresholds, MNI coordinates, tables and figures are provided). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This study uses fMRI with a social task (cyberball) and includes a separately reported healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 met). However, the full text does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group (i.e., a HC within-group/main-effect whole-brain map). The paper reports between-group contrasts (BPD vs HC, NSSI vs HC) and conjunctions but does not provide a standalone healthy-group whole-brain task effect in the manuscript (I5 not met). Therefore exclusion criterion E4 applies: the study reports primarily between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Exclusion rationale: E4 met; Inclusion met: I3, I4; Inclusion not met: I5.

This is a task-based fMRI study of animacy perception (a form of Perception/Understanding of Others) using healthy adult participants (fMRI cohorts: 20 per group, ages 19–36). The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (conjunction contrasts, FWE-corrected maps) with coordinates and tables, and describes results in text/figures. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I6 (results reported in acceptable formats). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It uses task-based fMRI with multiple social-related tasks (false belief, intentional/animacy triangles, voice/emotion recognition, eyes intention, trustworthiness) (I3). The sample is 78 healthy adults (age range 18–40, mean 23.5) with results reported for the healthy group (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses (RFX) across 78 subjects with voxelwise FWE-corrected thresholding and provides peak coordinates and maps (I5; I6). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, and healthy-group whole-brain task effects are provided. Therefore the study should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (observation of dynamic facial expressions — social communication/perception of others) in a healthy adult sample (n=51, ages within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects task analyses (one-sample t tests and ANOVAs) with family-wise error correction across the whole brain and reports activation foci and maps in the text/tables/figures. Thus it satisfies I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, age range appropriate, and empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion met: E2 (study reports ROI-based connectivity/graph-theoretical analyses without any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map). Inclusion not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain/voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy group are reported). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=31, mean age 24.3) that implemented social tasks (take-advice game and subsequent trust game) targeting social cognition and trust. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results: univariate whole-brain contrasts (voxel/FWE-corrected results, cluster tables) and whole-brain searchlight MVPA and LOSOCV classification/prediction analyses, with coordinates and supplementary tables. Whole-brain maps and coordinates are clearly described for the healthy/control group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, MRI acquisition, preprocessing, GLMs), Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is included in the review.

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria. It uses task-based fMRI to compare vocal (socially relevant) versus non-vocal sounds, addressing social communication/perception. Participants are healthy adults within the 18–65 range (Experiments: n=13, mean age 26.6; n=18, mean age 23.1), satisfying sample requirements. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (vocal > non-vocal and related maps) with voxelwise thresholds, cluster extents, and MNI coordinates (figures and peak coordinates provided), fulfilling whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and is empirical).

The article reports task-based fMRI during a social-related task (observation of socio-affective touch videos) and uses appropriate analyses (univariate and MVPA). It includes a matched neurotypical healthy adult control group (21 NT adults) with results reported separately. The paper provides group-level whole-brain task-evoked results for the healthy group (mean group effects, figures and tables of peak coordinates in Additional file 1: Figure S2 and Table S2), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Full article text (background, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, only between-group contrasts without healthy-group maps, age outside range, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore this study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=24, ages 22–39) that investigates social-related processing (collective memory and social schemas) and reports both region-of-interest and whole-brain analyses. The task involved recall of museum pictures prompting retrieval of collective/social knowledge; analyses explicitly test representation of collective (social) schemas in dmPFC/vmPFC. The paper includes group-level, whole-brain searchlight analyses with TFCE permutation correction and reports whole-brain results (Extended Data Fig. 1), satisfying the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met, and no exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).
